notes: All eight tools are registered unconditionally in the ListTools handler (dist/index.js:390-404); there is no flag or toolset gating, so every tool is default-enabled once the two required env vars are present.

All network calls go to fixed `https://slack.com/api/...` endpoints (dist/index.js:175,184,197,208,220,236,244,255,265); no agent-supplied URL or host is ever fetched, so the SINK labels rest solely on agent-chosen Slack channel/thread recipients for message posting.
No filesystem, shell or subprocess use anywhere in the file, so no tool is HOSTEXEC.

slack_add_reaction.rationale: `addReaction` only sends an emoji `name` plus channel/timestamp to the fixed Slack `reactions.add` endpoint and returns the API ack; it reads no workspace content back and carries no meaningful agent-supplied payload to an attacker-readable destination.

slack_get_channel_history.rationale: `getChannelHistory` fetches `conversations.history` with the user's bot credentials and returns raw message JSON to the agent: private workspace conversation content (SECRET) that is authored by many parties - other members, guests, Slack Connect/external users, and bots/integrations relaying web content - so the text is attacker-influencable (UNTRUSTED).

slack_get_thread_replies.rationale: `getThreadReplies` returns raw `conversations.replies` JSON read with the bot token: non-public workspace messages (SECRET) whose bodies are written by third parties including external/guest users and relay bots (UNTRUSTED).

slack_get_user_profile.rationale: `getUserProfile` calls `users.profile.get` with the bot token and returns the detailed profile JSON (SECRET). Profile text is authored by the target user, who may be an external/guest account rather than the operator, so it is treated as attacker-influencable; the code cannot rule this out.

slack_get_users.rationale: `getUsers` reads `users.list` with the user's bot token and returns the full member directory (names, emails, profile fields) into context - non-public workspace data. Profile fields are self-authored by arbitrary workspace members including guests/Slack Connect users, so the returned strings may carry injected instructions; kept as UNTRUSTED under the least-restrictive reading since the code does not constrain who may be in the directory.

slack_list_channels.rationale: `getChannels` calls Slack `conversations.list` / `conversations.info` with the user's bot token (`botHeaders`, dist/index.js:158-161) and returns the raw JSON into the agent context, exposing non-public workspace channel metadata (names, topics, purposes). No agent-chosen outbound destination, so no SINK; channel topics/purposes are member-authored but the primary reach here is workspace metadata.

slack_post_message.rationale: `postMessage` posts agent-supplied `text` to an agent-chosen `channel_id` via `chat.postMessage`; the recipient channel is fully chosen by the agent and may be a public, shared or Slack Connect channel readable by an attacker, so arbitrary agent data can be delivered outward.

slack_reply_to_thread.rationale: `postReply` sends agent-supplied `text` to an agent-chosen `channel_id`/`thread_ts` through `chat.postMessage`, the same attacker-reachable delivery path as posting a message.

value_conditions.default: unset - all public channels in the team are listed
value_conditions.effect: Restricts `slack_list_channels` to the listed channels via `conversations.info` instead of enumerating all public channels; it does not restrict the channel_id accepted by history/reply/post tools, so SINK and SECRET reach is unchanged.

value_conditions.default: unset - process exits with an error
value_conditions.effect: Both are required; if either is missing the server exits before advertising any tool, so no tool is reachable.
